newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. border remains closed after Manitoba blizzard.
newsitem.headline: U.S. border remains closed after Manitoba blizzard.

text.p: A four-lane highway linking Manitoba to Minnesota and North Dakota remained closed for a third day due to blizzard conditions, but Winnipeg's airport reopened at 0330 CDT/0930 GMT, officials said.

"I doubt the roads will be open until this afternoon. There were white-out conditions and cars stopped on the highways and other vehicles came behind them and crashed into them," Royal Canadian Mounted Police Sgt. Gerry Jennings said.
Hundreds of cars were abandoned in and around Winnipeg but only a few injuries were reported, Jennings said.
More than 35 cm (14 inches) of snow fell over the weekend with winds up to 80 km/h (50 mph), Environment Canada said.
"I'm not aware of fatalities at this point but I'm sure this is the kind of condition that would lend itself to that," Jennings added.
Highway 75 to the U.S. border, the TransCanada Highway to Ontario and other minor highways remained closed, he said.
Five hundred trucks transit the Hwy. 75 crossing each day.
Winnipeg International Airport reopened at 0330 CDT/0930 GMT on Monday after the blizzard conditions forced its closure 24 hours earlier, duty manager Doug Poole said.
Sixty Air Canada flights were diverted, stranding about 2,000 passengers, an airline official said.
Canadian Airlines Corp officials were not immediately available for comment.
Trains were running but were delayed by the weather.
"There's been some impact in Winnipeg and the Prairie area but not in the (United) States," CP Rail System spokesman Steve Morris said.
"The concern in St. Paul-Minneapolis is flooding, which is supposed to peak Wednesday," Morris said.
CP Rail runs the SOO Line from Winnipeg to Minneapolis.
Canadian National Railway Co officials were not immediately available for comment.

Forecasts last month showed Manitoba faced a 10 percent chance of the worst spring flooding of the century this spring but the blizzard will force a revision of that projection, Manitoba Natural Resources manager of Water Planning and Development Larry Whitney said.
All public schools in Winnipeg were closed for the day.
Normal snow accumulation for Winnipeg since October 1 is 104.8 cm (41.26 inches), but accumulation to date this winter reached 205.8 cm (81.02 inches), Environment Canada said.
